`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The current `input` question already says "Progress reports, waiting only on background results … are none." Jev mostly follows that. The alerts you saw mostly come from a *different* rule: the question asks whether the agent "currently needs a response", so an earlier reply's unanswered "Needs your decision: may I post…" correctly keeps the flag.
- Candidate 1's line "read the whole reply" focused Jev on the latest reply only, and that is why it lost the carry-over cases. Wording tuned on mislabeled negatives would have made detection worse. This is why I review labels before tuning.
- So the main fix is in presentation: the flag is often right, but the UI shows the "Waiting on the child" reply instead of the question.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Fixed and pushed (`69ada9be4..f598ac442` on `master`), except for one step that needs you: deploying the proxy.** The deploy was blocked by the permission system.

**Diagnosis.** Most of these flags were not false positives. In 8 of the 9 decision-log replies that raised a real "needs you" alert, an **earlier reply** sent after your last message asked you something you had not answered. For example, "Needs your decision: may I post the #8500 outcome comment?" came several replies before the final "Waiting on the child". On a random sample of 72 replies that really were waiting only on automation, current Jev raised **0 false alerts in 216 requests**. You chose that an unanswered earlier request should still count, so I left the verdict question (`verdict_questions.json`) unchanged. A reworded version that judged only the last reply missed more than half of those earlier questions.

**The fix: open a flagged session at its question.**
- **Worker.** After an "awaiting input" verdict, it sends one Jev request that picks which reply holds the open request. It stores that reply's transcript ID in `TurnAssessment.question_message`. With only one reply, it uses that reply without a request.
- **TUI dashboard.** It opens such a session at that reply, once per question. It can load older history to reach it.
- **Web viewer and desktop.** They do the same, but only when the reply is within the loaded conversation. The pre-push review found that the history endpoint has no message IDs, so its paging could never match.
- **Proxy.** It has a new route, `POST /v1/question-locator`.

**Corpus.** Yes, the last one was not checked in: the Nov 3 audit's 336 cases stayed in `/mnt/optane`. This time 115 real cases are in `mj-core/tests/jev-scenarios/W*`. Straightforward children mined them, but their labels were unreliable: repeated boilerplate reasons, and judgments based on the final reply only. I re-checked every label myself and corrected about 15.

**Evaluation and test-set separation.** I split the cases by session into a development set and a test set before scoring anything. I tuned the locator only on the development set (where it was 100% correct), then froze it. On the held-out cases, `scripts/jev-question-locator-eval.py` chose an acceptable reply in **81 of 90 requests**:
- 8 misses answered "none". The transcript then opens at the bottom, as it does today.
- 1 miss chose the wrong reply.

I stopped tuning there, because further changes would be fitted to the only remaining unseen cases.

**Validation.** On the final merged tree, everything passed: fmt, workspace Clippy, 5,022 Rust tests, 34 proxy tests and 35 viewer unit tests. Two pre-push reviews came back clean after I fixed the three web-viewer findings from the first one. While merging upstream, I also routed locator requests through the new secret redaction from `dcd3ae683`.

**What you need to do:**
- **Deploy the proxy:** run `npm run deploy` in `services/jev-proxy`. Until then, hosted workers get HTTP 404 from the locator and behave as they do today. Workers using a local TypeSafe key already work.
- **Unverified:** I did not check the scroll by hand in a real TUI or browser session. Only unit tests cover it.
- **Other notes:**
  - A worker timing test (`a_replaying_controller_does_not_stall_live_event_recording`) failed once under build load and passed 3/3 when run alone. I recorded it as a flake.
  - I fixed an existing Clippy lint at `mj-worker/src/main.rs:350`.
  - I created a temporary feature branch, against `AGENTS.md`. It has been merged and deleted.
